title: Machine learning predicts beer flavor and consumer appreciation from chemistry
summary: Over 200 chemical properties, trained-panel sensory scores and data from over 180,000 consumer reviews for 250 beers were used to train 10 machine-learning models; Gradient Boosting performed best and outperformed conventional statistics. Model analysis identified compounds driving flavor and appreciation, and adding them produced commercial alcoholic and non-alcoholic beer variants with improved consumer appreciation.
ai_technology: Ten machine-learning models, best Gradient Boosting, on chemical, sensory and consumer-review data
organization: VIB-KU Leuven Center for Microbiology; KU Leuven; Leuven Institute for Beer Research

evidence.tested: Blending of identified compounds into commercial beers followed by tasting and consumer appreciation assessment.
evidence.unknown: Effect sizes and tasting panel design not stated in the abstract; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Models predicted flavor and appreciation and model dissection flagged compounds to add.
